newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai military pledges full support for new premier.
newsitem.headline: Thai military pledges full support for new premier.

text.p: Thailand's military on Tuesday gave an unprecedented show of support for an elected government by pledging full cooperation with former army chief turned premier, Chavalit Yongchaiyudh, military officials said.
Chavalit received the backing of the armed service chiefs on his front lawn after officially being appointed the 22nd prime minister by royal decree late on Monday.

The military has orchestrated 17 coups or attempted coups since Thailand abandoned its absolute monarchy for parliamentary democracy in 1932 and is usually reluctant to show its support for elected politicians, analysts say.
It recently vowed to stay neutral.
More than 1,000 soldiers led by supreme commander General Mongkol Ampornpisith marched to Chavalit's house early on Tuesday to pledge support for his six-party coalition.

"General Chavalit was the supreme commander and army commander in chief, who turned politician and won the election that makes him the graceful prime minister," Mongkol, accompanied by the army, navy and air force commanders, told Chavalit on the lawn.
"On behalf of the military we are here to pledge our full support to cooperate with you and your government in all aspects," he said.
Chavalit was military chief from 1987 to 1989 before leaving to form the New Aspiration Party (NAP) in 1990.

The NAP scored a two-seat victory over the Democrat Party in the November 17 general elections. Chavalit formed a six-party coalition that will command 221 seats in the 393-seat lower house of parliament.
The military pledged neutrality during the election despite allegations that generals close to Chavalit were sent out to intimidate supporters of rival parties.
Chavalit told his well-wishers he would always be a soldier in his heart.
"For the the rest of my life, I will never forget that I was from the military and am a life-long soldier," he said.

Chavalit, due to be sworn in along with his cabinet by King Bhumibol Adulyadej on December 1, will be only the second elected prime minister in Thai history to make the transition without the intervention of a military coup.
In February 1991, the military staged a bloodless coup to topple the elected government of prime minister Chatichai Choonhavan.
Chatichai now leads Chart Pattana Party, which won 52 seats in the election and is the second largest party in Chavalit's coalition.
He is expected to play a powerful role in the new government and is likely to oversee several portfolios, including foreign affairs, industry, communications and transport.
